_meta.indication: Add-on maintenance treatment of patients with severe asthma aged 12 years and older, and with an eosinophilic phenotype

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, dose-ranging; 52 weeks
pivotal_trials.population: Severe asthma with eosinophilic inflammation and a history of 2 or more exacerbations in the previous year despite high-dose ICS plus an additional controller
pivotal_trials.result: Mepolizumab 75 mg IV reduced exacerbations to 1.24/yr vs placebo 2.40/yr; rate ratio 0.52 (95% CI 0.39, 0.69)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 32-week exacerbation trial evaluating 100 mg SC and 75 mg IV
pivotal_trials.population: Adults and adolescents ≥12 years with severe asthma (high-dose ICS plus additional controller), ≥2 exacerbations in the prior year, enriched for blood eosinophils ≥300 cells/µL in prior 12 months or ≥150 cells/µL at screening
pivotal_trials.n: N=576 (NUCALA 100 mg SC 194, mepolizumab 75 mg IV 191, placebo 191)
pivotal_trials.result: NUCALA 100 mg SC reduced exacerbations to 0.83/yr vs placebo 1.74/yr; rate ratio 0.47 (95% CI 0.35, 0.64); mepolizumab 75 mg IV rate ratio 0.53 (95% CI 0.40, 0.72)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study MEA115575 (Study 75; labeled Trial 3; steroid-reduction study)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, parallel-group, 24-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with asthma requiring daily oral corticosteroids in addition to high-dose ICS plus an additional controller to maintain asthma control; no exacerbation history required
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent reduction of oral corticosteroid dose during Weeks 20 to 24 vs baseline while maintaining asthma control
pivotal_trials.result: Greater OCS dose reduction with NUCALA; odds ratio to placebo 2.39 (95% CI 1.25, 4.56), p=0.008

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) were headache (19% vs 18% placebo), injection site reaction (8% vs 3%), back pain (5% vs 4%), and fatigue (5% vs 4%); hypersensitivity reactions and herpes zoster infections (2 serious cases vs none in placebo) are warnings
target_moa: Mepolizumab is a humanized interleukin-5 (IL-5) antagonist monoclonal antibody (IgG1 kappa) that binds to IL-5, blocking its binding to the alpha chain of the IL-5 receptor on eosinophils; IL-5 is the major cytokine responsible for growth, differentiation, recruitment, activation, and survival of eosinophils
modality: mAb (humanized IL-5 antagonist monoclonal antibody, IgG1 kappa)

rems.type: No REMS was proposed and none will be required

advisory_committee.vote: Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) June 11, 2015; voting questions were broken down by age – adults 18 years and older, and pediatrics 12 to 17 years; committee voted for approval in adults 18 years and older (14 Yes, 0 No) but against approval in pediatrics 12 to 17 years (4 Yes, 10 No)
